name: Latxa 3.1 (Llama-3.1 8B / 70B continually pretrained and instruction-tuned for Basque)
links: HF: HiTZ/Latxa-Llama-3.1-8B (base), HiTZ/Latxa-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (experimental variants stored as branches), HiTZ/Latxa-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct; collection huggingface.co/collections/HiTZ/latxa-instruct. Paper: Sainz et al., 'Instructing Large Language Models for Low-Resource Languages: A Systematic Study for Basque', arXiv:2506.07597, EMNLP 2025 (aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.1484). Code: github.com/hitz-zentroa/latxa-instruct. Predecessor: Latxa (Llama 2, 7B-70B), Etxaniz et al., ACL 2024. Relevant NLI evaluations: XNLIeu (Heredia et al., NAACL 2024, github.com/hitz-zentroa/xnli-eu); 'Lost in Variation' (CoNLL 2025, arXiv:2506.15239).
license_access: Open-weight under the Llama 3.1 Community License (commercial and research use allowed, Meta acceptable-use policy and attribution apply). Also served by third-party inference providers (e.g. Featherless) but self-hosting is the normal route.
track_coverage: Primarily T3 EU and EU-containing T4 mixed views; usable on T1 EN / T2 ES since it inherits Llama-3.1's English/Spanish ability (instruct data mixes Basque and English), but the model card warns performance outside Basque is not guaranteed, so plain Llama-3.1 / Qwen3 etc. are the better choice for T1/T2.
basque_quality: Strongest open Basque LLM family. 8B-Instruct vs Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (5-shot): Belebele 80.00 vs 73.89, X-StoryCloze 71.34 vs 61.22, EusProficiency 52.83 vs 34.13, EusReading 62.78 vs 49.72, EusTrivia 61.05 vs 45.01, EusExams 56.00 vs 46.21. 70B-Instruct: Belebele 91.00, X-StoryCloze 77.83, EusProficiency 68.00, EusReading 78.98, EusTrivia 74.17, EusExams 71.56; ranked 3rd in a Basque human-preference arena behind Claude and GPT-4o-class models, above all other same-size open models. No XNLIeu number for Latxa 3.1 found [uncertain]; the earlier Latxa-7B (Llama 2) scored only 50.9 zero-shot on XNLIeu (53.3 native), and Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct with CoT got 60.71 on XNLIeu-native vs 83.8 for fine-tuned XLM-R-large (translate-train), i.e. prompting lags fine-tuned encoders on Basque NLI by a wide margin.
cross_lingual_robustness: Good in principle: a single decoder sees both phrases in one prompt and was trained on Basque + English (Llama-3.1 base also covers Spanish), so EU-EN / EU-ES mixed pairs should degrade less than for monolingual encoders. Continual Basque pretraining may slightly erode English/Spanish quality [uncertain: magnitude not reported in the sources checked]. Prompting results are also sensitive to the prompt language.
architecture: Decoder-only Llama-3.1 transformer (GQA, RoPE, 128k-vocab tiktoken tokenizer, 128k context) continually pretrained on Latxa Corpus v1.1 (4.3M documents, 4.2B Basque tokens) then instruction-tuned on ~1M Magpie-style synthetic Basque/English instructions (+ preference data). Two usage modes for DiCo: (a) LoRA fine-tuning with a classification head (LlamaForSequenceClassification: last-token pooled hidden state -> 4-way linear) or restricted-vocabulary label-token scoring; (b) zero/few-shot prompting of the Instruct model with label definitions, scoring the four label tokens' log-probs.
compute: 8B: LoRA in bf16 fits 24 GB for short phrase-pair inputs (~16 GB weights + adapters/activations; tight) or comfortably with QLoRA 4-bit (~8-12 GB); an epoch over 3k rows is minutes, over T4's 18k rows ~15-30 min on an A100/H100. 70B: QLoRA needs ~45-50 GB+ -> one 80 GB GPU (A100/H100) or multi-GPU; full bf16 inference needs ~140 GB (2x80 GB) or 4-bit ~40 GB. Official training used 4 A100-64GB nodes (16k GPU hours for 70B instruct), irrelevant for adaptation.
sample_efficiency: LoRA-tuned LLM classifiers are generally more sample-efficient than encoders trained from MLM weights because of strong priors, and ~1.3k reversible pairs (3k rows) is a workable LoRA regime; expected seed variance is moderate (LoRA init + data order) [uncertain]. Zero/few-shot prompting needs no training data but, on prior Basque NLI evidence, underperforms fine-tuned models by 15-30 accuracy points; few-shot with 8-16 in-context examples helps modestly.
reported_results: Latxa 3.1 benchmarks (5-shot): see basque_quality (8B Belebele 80.00, 70B 91.00, etc.). NLI-specific evidence (other Latxa/Llama versions): XNLIeu zero-shot prompting Latxa-7B (Llama 2) 50.9 (XNLIeuMT 47.8, native 53.3) vs BLOOM-7B 49.8 native, XGLM 48.1; fine-tuned XLM-R-large 83.8 translate-train / 81.1 zero-shot transfer (Heredia et al., NAACL 2024). Lost in Variation (CoNLL 2025): Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct CoT XNLIeu-native 60.71 -> var 49.22; Gemma-2-27B-it 66.99 -> 58.05; Spanish native 77.29 (Llama-70B). A Latxa-3.1-8B vs Llama-3.1-8B evaluation on Iberian tasks reports Latxa slightly better on XNLI-based NLI and worse on WNLI (arXiv:2504.03312) [uncertain: exact numbers not retrieved]. No LoRA-classification or phrase-level NLI / DiCo results for Latxa exist.
pilot_dico_results: Not evaluated. The LREC 2026 pilot was English-only and its decoder-only family (e.g. OPT-125M: 0.61 / 0.65 / 0.58; family avg 0.583 / 0.568 / 0.498) was the weakest, but those were tiny decoders and do not bound an 8B/70B LoRA model.
consistency_guarantee: none by default; inference-time consistency is possible by scoring both directions (or a single joint prompt that outputs a label pair) and decoding over consistent label pairs.
negative_other_handling: As a classifier head: NEG is one of 4 outputs and can be emitted on only one direction of a reversible pair. As a prompted model: NEG must be defined carefully in the prompt ('unrelated, contradictory, or partially overlapping'); LLMs tend to over-predict entailment/equivalence for loosely related phrases or over-use 'other' depending on wording [uncertain]. Best combined with a pair-level NEG gate and joint decoding.
metric_tradeoff: LoRA-8B classifier: plausibly competitive with XLM-R-large on T3 W-F1 and a strong, diverse ensemble member [uncertain]; SoftCons/HardCons governed by decoding. Prompting: low W-F1 (NLI prompting in Basque is weak), but a joint two-direction prompt can yield high SoftCons; not a good primary system. 70B LoRA may add a few W-F1 points over 8B at much higher cost.
integration: Custom path beyond the encoder pipeline: AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained('HiTZ/Latxa-Llama-3.1-8B', num_labels=4, torch_dtype=bfloat16) + peft LoraConfig(task_type='SEQ_CLS', r=16, target q/k/v/o[/gate/up/down]), set tokenizer.pad_token = eos and model.config.pad_token_id; format input as a short template ('Esaldia A: ... Esaldia B: ...' or English template) so the last token summarizes the pair. Alternatively a causal-LM head restricted to 4 label tokens. For prompting, serve the Instruct model with vLLM and read label-token log-probs (not free text) to get per-class probabilities; run both directions for reversal aggregation via REVERSE_PERM.
ensemble_compatibility: Yes for the LoRA classifier (softmax over 4 labels; temperature-scale on dev). Prompted label-token log-probs are usable but poorly calibrated - calibrate (e.g. contextual calibration / temperature) before pooling.
inference_cost: 8B classifier: ~1-3 min for ~4k rows x 2 directions on one GPU. 70B: ~10-30 min with vLLM on 2x80 GB (or 4-bit on one 80 GB) for label-token scoring; more with CoT generation.
rules_disclosure: Disclose: open-weight, decoder-only (Llama-3.1 family, Basque-adapted), fine-tuning (LoRA) and/or prompt engineering, few-shot examples, external data if any intermediate NLI training (e.g. XNLIeu), ensembling. Comply with the Llama 3.1 license (attribution 'Built with Llama', acceptable-use policy).
contamination: Llama-3.1 pretraining (15T web tokens) likely contains the public English iSTS/PhrasIS source sentences and possibly the PhrasIS release itself (public since ~2021) [uncertain]; Latxa Corpus v1.1 (Basque news/web) is unlikely to contain the new DiCo Basque translations. Latxa instruct data is synthetic (Magpie) and not NLI-targeted. Label leakage risk is low but should be disclosed per the pending PhrasIS policy.
structural_cue_dependence: No for the model itself; joint two-direction prompting or pair decoding relies on knowing the reversed twin (available via id convention), which is a decoding-layer assumption.
priority: P1 for LoRA 8B classification on T3/T4 (after XLM-R/mDeBERTa baselines); P2 for zero/few-shot prompting and for 70B.
expected_gain: Main upside is Basque-side competence plus LLM priors for T3 and EU-containing T4 views: a LoRA-tuned Latxa-8B could match or exceed XLM-R-large on T3 and add ensemble diversity (+1-2 W-F1 in an ensemble is a reasonable guess) [uncertain]. Prompting alone is expected to be clearly worse than fine-tuned encoders (prior Basque NLI prompting 50-67% vs ~76-84% fine-tuned), so its use is as a pseudo-labeler or weak ensemble member. 70B adds cost with uncertain marginal gain.
